author: Anja Wuolu
title: Golden Valley police chief resigns after investigation concludes - NewsBreak
text:
By Anja Wuolu ,
5 days ago
Golden Valley Police Chief Virgil Green has resigned, following the results of an external investigation.
Green was on administrative leave from May 28 until Oct. 1. Due to data privacy laws, the city could not release the reasons for his being put on leave until the completion of the investigation. On Oct. 1, the city reported that he'd resigned and released the results of the investigation.
The investigation looked at two main areas of misconduct: interfering with an internal investigation and releasing private data.
Interference with investigation
The city of Golden Valley contracted with Michelle M. Soldo from Attorney & Investigator Soldo Consulting, P.C. to investigate whether Green interfered with an internal investigation in the spring.
Green was informed of one officer's possible misconduct on April 2.
Based on the training Green had attended in November and January, the Soldo report states Green should have informed in the city manager and attorney of the allegations.
Instead, Green made "multiple attempts to quash and then downplay," told the person who made the complaint of misconduct that they could not talk to the city attorney and "sent objectively threatening emails."
"Multiple witnesses confirmed that the Chief made statements indicating he did not want to involve City Hall, HR and the Minnesota POST Board," the Soldo report reads.
Upper management only learned of the situation when an anonymous person contacted the city attorney, 19 days later. Because of data practices laws, details of the officer's alleged misconduct are redacted. What is public information, is how Green handled this situation:
"Chief Green improperly interfered in the GVPD’s internal investigation of the alleged [redacted], attempting to quash the investigation by intimidation directives and side dealing, conduct that contravenes City policies and state law," the investigation report reads.
Releasing private data
Per previous Sun reporting, the GVPD had responded to a 911 call of two female students fighting at Robbinsdale Academy - Highview in Golden Valley. Despite video proof of brass knuckles being involved in the incident, Assistant Principal Patrick Burrage had told officers that the weapon was not used. Green asked for felony-level investigation interference charges, but the Hennepin County Attorney's Office declined to prosecute.
The aspect of the investigation that concerned the city was that Green released the full body-worn camera footage of the incident to district officials and the press.
"Chief Green confirmed that, at least twice prior to January 21, 2025, he showed to Robbinsdale School District officials, unredacted BWC video related to an active criminal investigation. On or about January 21, 2025, Chief Green showed and released the same BWC video to KSTP and he gave an on-camera interview to KSTP in which he discussed details of the case," the Soldo report reads.
Per the report, Green said an admin employee told him he “[has] the discretion and knows what images can and cannot be shown.”
Green also was said to be "under the impression that public employees performing their duties had no expectation of privacy, so redaction of the content of the BWC video was not required."
The Soldo investigation cites state law, saying, “[i]nactive investigative data are public unless the release of the data would jeopardize another ongoing investigation or would reveal the identity of individuals protected under subdivision 17.”
The Soldo investigation states that Green "never intended to violate any City policy or State statute," and that he learned his lesson.
However, the Soldo investigation concludes that this remained a breach of data privacy rights.
Future of GVPD
Assistant chiefs Alice White and Rudy Perez co-led the Golden Valley Police Department during Green’s administrative leave and will continue to do so as the city selects an interim chief.
“Chief Green joined us at a critical time, and we thank him for all he did for the City of Golden Valley, its police force and the community in his time here,” City Manager Noah Schuchman said. “We will be sharing details regarding the search for a new Chief of Police soon. I want to thank Assistant Chiefs White and Perez for their leadership and commitment over the past few months.”
